quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: Indicates that the driver sees you.
Doesn't mean that the driver will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that the other driver will properly yield to you.
May make the driver mad.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Don't rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but still don't see them.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from the elements
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting the distance ridden in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks on long trips. Don't ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Never use artificial stimulants—they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Assume the motorcycle is as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers can't see you.
Not be concerned with taking steps to ensure that other drivers see you.
Ride offensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers can't see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have smaller lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors on your motorcycle?

options.text: Most people aren't used to using mirrors.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look closer than they really are.
It can be difficult to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unlike flat mirrors, they make items look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What is true about brightly-colored helmets?

options.text: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
Can be distracting.
Don't help to improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire provides the power for the bike, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely leave the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the stop sign then proceed through the intersection.
Ignore the stop sign and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop sign before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, stop first. Then move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad.

questions.question: Which statement about a windshield is true?

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
About 95 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day in similar conditions.
The same speed as you would during the day in similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day in similar conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day in similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Slowing down helps you avoid accidents.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
When you need to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's single brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see it, especially when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: What should you do to make a quick stop on wet pavement?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use both brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes for a quick stop on a slippery surface. Apply the front brake gradually to prevent it from locking.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When the pavement is dry.
When the pavement is wet.
When you can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
When the sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. This includes wet or slippery pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and stop using it.
Release the front brake, then quickly squeeze it again.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This position gives you the best view of the passing lane.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see all traffic around you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should motorcyclists do about space cushions?

options.text: They do not need space cushions.
They should increase their space cushions.
They should reduce their space cushions by half.
They should maintain adequate space cushions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should maintain adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle in front of you under normal conditions. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: What can help if your motorcycle chain slips?

options.text: Tightening the chain
Loosening the chain
Using more throttle
Applying the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Tightening the chain
questions.explanation: Try tightening the chain if it slips. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle thoroughly?

options.text: It is useless unless a mechanic does it
You should not check it before a ride
You should only check it after a ride
It helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment that could be dangerous.

questions.question: How should you check tire pressure?

options.text: By looking at the tire
Use a tire gauge
By squeezing the tire
By comparing it to another tire's height

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that is under-inflated can still look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery road?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced
Keep your speed up to improve traction
Do not worry about road conditions
Keep your motorcycle upright and go slowly

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go slowly
questions.explanation: Try to avoid slippery roads. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and ride as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It lets you see farther ahead
It blocks your view ahead
It makes it hard to see the vehicle ahead
It lets the other driver speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see farther ahead
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when passing to see farther ahead and to make yourself more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help protect you from serious injury?

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet
Face or eye protection
Ear buds
Protective clothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a strong jacket and pants, boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not protect you from injury.

questions.question: When a group passes another vehicle, what should the riders do?

options.text: Let one rider finish passing before the next one starts
Have several riders pass at the same time
Have the last rider wave to signal no more bikes are coming
Pass in a staggered formation

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider finish passing before the next one starts
questions.explanation: Group riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should complete their pass and return to the group formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: What happens to traction when you are turning?

options.text: You have less grip for stopping
You have more grip for stopping
Stopping is the same as on a straight road
You should never try to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less grip for stopping
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be careful. When leaning to turn, some traction is used for the turn, leaving less available for stopping.
